input.justification: The tainted request parameter is passed into Test.doSomething(), which inserts it into a List alongside two constant strings ["safe", param, "moresafe"], then calls valuesList.remove(0) (removing the first "safe" element) and returns valuesList.get(1). After the removal, index 1 of the list is the constant "moresafe", not the user-supplied value. So `bar` returned by doSomething() is always the literal string "moresafe" regardless of the parameter's value, and the subsequent fileName = TESTFILES_DIR + bar used in the FileInputStream/FileOutputStream sink is therefore not influenced by user input. The dataflow CodeQL reports is overestimated due to imprecise handling of List.remove()/get() index semantics; the actual runtime value reaching the sink is a fixed constant, so there is no exploitable path traversal here.
